description: FALSIFIER (closure predicate, in summary because substrateGap_write discards a free-text falsifier): the condition in which a transport advertises a /p2p-circuit multiaddr that the relay answers with NO_RESERVATION is REPRODUCIBLE on demand, and a named local signal distinguishes it from a healthy node BEFORE an external peer fails to dial. || WHAT WAS OBSERVED, unattended, by federation-probe-tick: peer-fixture-1's transport self-reported activeReservations=1 and advertised a circuit multiaddr; an independent ephemeral peer dialling that circuit got 'failed to connect via relay with status NO_RESERVATION'; and the hub was still serving 7 of its rows as fresh. I8_cross_boundary_deadvertise failed with stale_foreign_rows_advertised and I4_forced_relay failed with relay_dial_failed, both naming that peer. A transport restart restored reachability. || WHAT WAS FIXED: activeReservations counts /p2p-circuit LISTEN ADDRESSES, which the listener can hold after the reservation behind them is gone. /health now also reports reservationsHeld — the circuit-relay-v2 client's own ReservationStore map, emptied on relay:removed — plus the relay peer, the reservation expiry, and a phantomSuspected flag when a listen address exists with zero held reservations. The phantom watchdog now redials immediately on that combination instead of waiting two strikes on quiet traffic. || WHAT IS STILL UNKNOWN, AND WHY THIS STAYS OPEN: the mechanism was NOT reproduced. Killing a relay under a live node made BOTH numbers fall to 0 together within ~10s — a clean shutdown is handled correctly. So the path that produced peer1's phantom is unidentified, and it remains entirely possible that its reservationsHeld also read 1, i.e. the CLIENT believed in a reservation the RELAY had forgotten. In that case the two signals agree and both are wrong, and the new field would not have caught it either. Claiming this fixed is not supportable from the evidence. || CANDIDATE MECHANISMS TO TEST: a relay RESTART while the client's TCP connection survives or is transparently re-established (the relay forgets reservations; the client does not); reservation TTL expiry on the relay side without a connection close; a half-open connection across a partition. The relay's keep-alive ping logs 'Protocol selection failed - could not negotiate /ipfs/ping/1.0.0' against some peers, which would prevent it detecting a dead reserved peer and may be the other half of the same story. || THE PRINCIPLE THIS SHARPENS: the client's own bookkeeping beats the listener's addresses, but it is still SELF-REPORT. The only authoritative check is an EXTERNAL DIAL — which is why the oracle caught this and the health endpoint did not, and why reachability verdicts are witnessed by the probe's own peer rather than by the subject.
